title: SQL JOINs Explained Simply
intro: JOINs combine rows from two or more tables. Pick the wrong one and you either lose data or duplicate it.

slides.heading: INNER JOIN
slides.subtitle: Only rows that match in both tables.
points: Returns rows where the join condition is true in both tables
Rows with no match on either side are excluded
examples: Orders that have a matching customer

slides.heading: LEFT JOIN
slides.subtitle: Everything from the left table, matched or not.
points: Keeps all rows from the left table
Unmatched right-side columns come back as NULL
examples: All customers, even those with zero orders

slides.heading: RIGHT JOIN
slides.subtitle: The mirror image of LEFT JOIN.
points: Keeps all rows from the right table
Unmatched left-side columns come back as NULL
Rarely used — most people rewrite it as a LEFT JOIN
examples: All products, even unordered ones, from the orders table

slides.heading: FULL JOIN
slides.subtitle: Everything from both tables.
points: Combines LEFT and RIGHT JOIN results
Unmatched rows from either side get NULLs
Good for finding mismatches between two tables
examples: Reconciling two systems that should be in sync
